estimate: Verification (STEP 0, five files + four docs): 3-4 hours, mandatory before coding. Rebrand of THIS surface only (marker file + keychain service + wsl-orca-env.ts + orca-profiles rename + migrations for the two silent-logout vectors): 1-2 days, dominated by migration safety rather than the renames. Claude api-key + custom-base-url auth modes on the existing env seam (STEP 3 + 4 + 5): 3-4 days. Binding resolution + spawn snapshot + live-pty-gate integration (STEP 6-7): 2-3 days. Codex parity via config.toml mirror (STEP 8): 4-6 days, the largest single chunk because of the mirror/trust/CODEX_HOME machinery — could shrink to 1-2 days if codex-model-provider-config.ts already covers it. UI (STEP 11): 2-3 days. Test churn against the existing ~27k-line subtree: 2-3 days. TOTAL 3-4 weeks for a shippable multi-account/API-config switcher, versus the 8-12 weeks it would take without the existing claude-accounts/codex-accounts foundation. The single biggest schedule risk is Codex, and the single biggest correctness risk is the two silent-logout migration vectors, both of which are cheap to handle if addressed before the rebrand lands.
gotchas: `.orca-managed-claude-auth` (managed-auth-path.ts) is a MARKER FILE CONTENT CONTRACT, not just a name. resolveOwnedClaudeManagedAuthPath() refuses to use any managed auth dir whose marker is missing or mismatched. Rename the constant and every existing user's accounts become unreadable — the function returns null and the app treats them as unowned. There is already an `adoptLegacyMarker` option, so the fix is to check the new name, then the old name, and rewrite. Looks like a one-line rename; is actually a data migration.

`ORCA_CLAUDE_SERVICE = 'Orca Claude Code Managed Credentials'` in keychain.ts is a macOS Keychain lookup key. Renaming it does not error — readManagedClaudeKeychainCredentials() just returns null, which the code path treats as 'no credentials', so users silently get logged out with no diagnostic. Must read both old and new service names during a transition window.

The Keychain service suffix is `sha256(configDir).hex.slice(0,8)`. Any change to the managed config dir PATH (including the userData relocation caused by the app rename) changes the hash and therefore the service name. Two independent rename levers converge on the same silent-logout failure.

`ACTIVE_CLAUDE_SERVICE = 'Claude Code-credentials'` must NOT be rebranded — it is Claude Code's own Keychain service, not this app's. Same for the OAuth client_id and token URL, and for the on-disk filenames '.credentials.json' and 'oauth-account.json'. A blind case-insensitive orca→aio-ide sweep is safe on these, but a broader 'clean up the strings' pass is not.

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR resolution has a subtle branch: runtime-paths.ts picks `<configDir>/.claude.json` when CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR was inherited OR when that colocated file already exists, otherwise `~/.claude.json`. A profile implementation that assumes config always lives beside credentials will read the wrong file for default/global accounts.

getRuntimePaths() calls mkdirSync(configDir, {recursive:true}) as a side effect of a getter. Calling it to 'just check' a path creates directories. Do not call it speculatively while enumerating profiles.

isAuthLikeCustomHeaders() strips ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS whenever it matches /authorization|x-api-key|api-key|bearer/i. A custom-base-url profile whose gateway requires an Authorization header will have that header silently removed — the exact use case the new feature exists to serve, defeated by an existing safety check.

src/main/claude-accounts/live-pty-gate.ts exists, which means the team already discovered that mutating account state under a running PTY is unsafe. Any profile edit/delete UI that does not consult this gate reintroduces a bug they have already fixed and tested (142-line test file).

src/main/codex/codex-pane-account-registry.ts + codex-pane-launch-account.ts + codex-stale-pane-accounts.ts mean per-session account binding ALREADY EXISTS for Codex, including stale-entry cleanup. Building a fresh per-session binding layer would duplicate working, tested code — and the 'stale pane accounts' module is evidence that lifecycle cleanup is the hard part they already solved.

src/main/codex/codex-model-provider-config.ts (+ test) may already implement custom base URLs for Codex. Read it before scoping the api-config work; the feature could be partly shipped for one provider and absent for the other, which changes the estimate substantially.

Codex custom-base-url cannot be delivered by env injection alone — it needs a model_provider block in config.toml inside the managed CODEX_HOME, routed through the existing mirror/upsert/runtime-owned-sections machinery. Treating both providers as 'just set two env vars' will produce a Claude implementation that works and a Codex one that silently ignores the profile.

src/main/pty/codex-home-wsl-env.ts (31 lines) exists solely to carry CODEX_HOME into WSL. Any new profile env var needs the same treatment or WSL-hosted agents will ignore the selected profile — and it will look like a profile-resolution bug rather than an env-bridging one.

skill-guides/orca-per-workspace-env.md carries a brand token in its filename AND is functionally load-bearing for per-workspace env. package.json has `verify:bundled-skill-guides` and `generate:bundled-skill-guides` scripts plus a skill-bundle manifest check, so renaming that file requires regenerating the bundle and manifest or `pnpm run lint` fails on verify:bundled-skill-guides.

`bin: {orca, orca-dev}` in package.json points at ./out/cli/index.js — the src/cli that is being deleted. Renaming the binary and deleting the CLI interact: there is a `verify:cli-bin` script that will fail if bin points at a nonexistent build output.

check:max-lines-ratchet is a lint gate, not advice. It ratchets, so adding a large new file can fail lint even though existing files are larger. Keep new profile modules small, consistent with the 34-233 line files already in src/main/claude-accounts/.

orderedSteps: STEP 0 — close the five verification gaps before writing any code. Read, in this order: (a) the pty:spawn IPC handler and its env assembly — find it with `rg -n "pty:spawn|ipcMain\\.handle\\('pty" src/main --glob '!*.test.ts'` then read the file plus src/main/pty/shell-startup-env.ts and src/main/pty/wsl-env.ts to locate any env allowlist/denylist; (b) src/main/ipc/settings.ts + settings.test.ts to answer the still-open zod/electron-store/sqlite and migration question; (c) src/main/claude-accounts/runtime-auth-service.ts (1806 lines) — the single highest-value unread file, it is where an account becomes a runtime env; (d) src/main/codex-accounts/runtime-home-service.ts (1780 lines) and src/main/codex/codex-model-provider-config.ts — the latter may already implement custom-base-url for Codex; (e) the four docs named in the brief. Do not design the settings slice before (b) and do not design the injection point before (a).

STEP 1 — inventory the auth-mode gap precisely. Run `rg -n --stats 'ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL|ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|OPENAI_BASE_URL|OPENAI_API_KEY' src` and classify each of the ~50 hits as (i) allowlist/strip membership, (ii) real feature code, (iii) test fixture, (iv) doc. My counts (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=2, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=12, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=11, OPENAI_API_KEY=17 vs CODEX_HOME=623) strongly imply BYO-key/gateway support is vestigial, but confirm before scoping.

STEP 2 — name the entity to avoid the two existing collisions (src/shared/orca-profiles.ts + src/main/pty/orca-profiles/, and src/shared/native-chat-agent-profiles.ts). Use `AgentAuthProfile` and a settings key `agentAuthProfiles`. Add the type to src/shared/ as a new file src/shared/agent-auth-profile.ts: {id: string; label: string; provider: 'claude'|'codex'; authMode: 'subscription-oauth'|'api-key'|'custom-base-url'; secretRef: string|null; baseUrl: string|null; modelDefaults: {model?: string; smallFastModel?: string}; createdAt: number}. secretRef is an opaque handle, never the secret itself — the secret lives in the store chosen in STEP 4.

STEP 3 — extend the env-injection seam rather than adding a parallel one. In src/main/claude-accounts/environment.ts widen ClaudeEnvPatch to {CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR?, ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS?, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL?, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN?, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY?, ANTHROPIC_MODEL?} and change applyClaudeEnvPatch so stripAuthEnv deletes only the auth vars the patch does NOT itself supply. Today it unconditionally deletes all four CLAUDE_AUTH_ENV_VARS and then only re-adds CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS, so an api-key profile injected through this function would have its key deleted. Also gate isAuthLikeCustomHeaders() so a custom-base-url profile that legitimately needs an Authorization header is not stripped. Add unit tests next to the existing ones.

STEP 4 — decide the secret-at-rest story explicitly, because keychain.ts is macOS-only (every function early-returns unless process.platform==='darwin'). Recommended: store secrets as 0600 files under app.getPath('userData')/agent-auth-profiles/<profileId>/, reusing the exact ownership contract already proven in src/main/claude-accounts/managed-auth-path.ts (marker file containing the id, symlink rejection, realpathSync containment, writeFileAtomically from codex-accounts/fs-utils.ts). Layer Electron safeStorage.encryptString over the file contents for defence in depth — safeStorage works on all three platforms whereas the `security` CLI does not. Read docs/windows-secure-file-acl-hardening.md first and apply the same ACL hardening. Do NOT put raw API keys in the general settings JSON.

STEP 5 — add the settings slice + migration using whatever mechanism STEP 0(b) reveals. Persist only non-secret profile metadata plus bindings: {profiles: AgentAuthProfile[], defaultProfileByProvider: Record<'claude'|'codex', string|null>, bindingsByWorkspace: Record<string, {claude?: string; codex?: string}>}. Migration must be additive with empty defaults so existing installs keep booting; adopt the current per-account state as an implicit 'subscription-oauth' profile per existing account so nobody sees an empty picker after upgrade.

STEP 6 — implement binding resolution as a pure function with an explicit precedence chain, in a new src/main/agent-auth-profile-resolution.ts: session/pane binding > worktree binding > workspace binding > provider default > legacy active account. Model it on the existing src/main/claude-accounts/runtime-selection.ts and src/main/codex-accounts/runtime-selection.ts, and for per-session binding generalise the already-working Codex mechanism in src/main/codex/codex-pane-account-registry.ts + codex-pane-launch-account.ts rather than inventing a new registry. Resolution must be pure and fully unit-tested — this is the correctness core.

STEP 7 — wire resolution into the spawn path found in STEP 0(a). Resolve the profile ONCE at spawn, snapshot {profileId, label, authMode, baseUrl, resolvedAt} onto the session record, and inject env from that snapshot. Never re-resolve mid-session. Respect the guard in src/main/claude-accounts/live-pty-gate.ts: mutating or deleting a profile that a live PTY is using must be blocked or deferred, exactly as that gate already does for accounts.

STEP 8 — Codex custom-base-url does NOT go through env alone. Codex reads model providers from config.toml, so a custom-base-url profile must write a model_provider block into the managed CODEX_HOME's config.toml via the existing mirror pipeline (src/main/codex/codex-config-mirror.ts, codex-config-settings-upsert.ts, codex-model-provider-config.ts, config-toml-runtime-owned-sections.ts). Use the runtime-owned-sections concept so the app's block is rewritten idempotently and never clobbers user-authored sections. Verify against codex-model-provider-config.test.ts — that test may already encode the required shape.

STEP 9 — do NOT mutate the user's global ~/.claude/.credentials.json, ~/.claude.json, or ~/.codex/auth.json as the switching mechanism. Reasons, all grounded in this codebase: (i) concurrent agents — this app runs many CLIs in parallel worktrees, so a global file has exactly one value and the last writer wins, whereas CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CODEX_HOME are per-process; (ii) clobbering — the CLI rewrites these files on its own schedule, so an app write races the CLI write with no lock; (iii) token-refresh races — refresh tokens are single-use, and oauth-refresh.ts's own comment calls scrape-back 'the lossy path that strands stale tokens'; two agents refreshing the same global blob invalidate each other's refresh token and log the user out; (iv) blast radius — a bug corrupts the user's real credentials, versus a throwaway managed dir. The env+managed-dir approach is already the architecture; keep it.

STEP 10 — implement the file-swap fallback narrowly and only where a CLI provably ignores env. Shape: materialise a complete managed config dir (the <profileId>/auth layout from managed-auth-path.ts), then point the CLI at it. Only if a CLI honours neither CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR nor CODEX_HOME should you consider touching the real home, and then it must be serialised behind a single-writer lock plus save/restore of the original file, and must refuse to run when any live PTY holds a different profile (reuse live-pty-gate.ts). Treat this as a last resort, feature-flagged, not the default.

STEP 11 — UI. Status-bar picker alongside the existing usage surface (src/shared/status-bar-usage-mode.ts, usage-percentage-display.ts) so quota and identity read together; a settings page for profile CRUD with a 'Test connection' action; and per-session provenance shown from the STEP 7 snapshot, so a running pane displays the profile it actually launched with even after the binding changes. Add the profile option to src/shared/agent-session-option-catalog-claude-codex.ts so it flows through the existing launch-options plumbing.

STEP 12 — tests and gates. This repo enforces `pnpm run lint` (oxlint + native/type-aware code-quality passes + check:reliability-gates + check:max-lines-ratchet), `pnpm run typecheck` across three tsconfigs, and `pnpm test` (vitest via config/vitest.config.ts). Note check:max-lines-ratchet: keep new files under the repo's per-file line ceiling — the CLAUDE.md guidance of ~200 lines matches the prevailing style in src/main/claude-accounts/ (environment.ts 52, runtime-paths.ts 34, managed-auth-path.ts 112, keychain.ts 233). Add focused unit tests for the widened applyClaudeEnvPatch, the pure resolution function, the settings migration, and the live-pty-gate interaction.
risks: Rebrand-vs-feature coupling: renaming the app changes app.getPath('userData'), which relocates the managed-accounts root that getClaudeManagedAccountsRoot() computes. Because keychain.ts scopes the Keychain service by sha256(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR).slice(0,8), and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR points inside userData for managed accounts, the rename ALSO changes every scoped Keychain service name. Rebrand and switcher must be sequenced deliberately, with a migration, or existing users silently lose all stored Claude accounts.

Scale of the existing subsystem: ~27,000 lines across the accounts/pty subtree, with test files larger than their implementations (runtime-home-service.ts 1780 vs its test 4544; runtime-auth-service.ts 1806 vs 3931). Any change to shared behaviour will break many tests. Budget for test churn, and do not weaken tests to pass.

I have not read the spawn path. If env for spawned agents flows through an allowlist (plausible given src/main/pty/wsl-env.ts and codex-home-wsl-env.ts exist specifically to bridge vars across the WSL boundary), then new profile vars will be silently dropped until added to that allowlist. This is the most likely 'it just doesn't work' failure at integration time.

macOS-only secret storage: keychain.ts no-ops on Windows and Linux, and this checkout is being developed on Windows 11. On the dev platform there is currently no OS-level secret protection for Claude credentials at all — only whatever file ACLs docs/windows-secure-file-acl-hardening.md describes. Shipping api-key profiles without safeStorage means plaintext keys on disk for most users.

Codex is not symmetrical with Claude. CODEX_HOME appears 623 times, there is a config mirror, a trust-grant ledger with telemetry, session backfill, index healing, and WSL hook install planning. A naive CODEX_HOME override will fight the mirror and trust reconciliation. Expect Codex profile work to cost 2-3x the Claude side.

OAuth values are pinned to an observed CLI version: oauth-refresh.ts hardcodes client_id 9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e and https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token, verified against claude 2.1.177 per its own comment. A CLI update can invalidate these. Same class of risk for the Keychain service name 'Claude Code-credentials' and the sha256-suffix scheme.

Stripping is currently unconditional: applyClaudeEnvPatch with stripAuthEnv deletes all four CLAUDE_AUTH_ENV_VARS and re-adds only CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS. Any api-key profile routed through it loses its key. This is a concrete bug you will hit on day one of STEP 3 if the widening is not done first.

Two pre-existing 'profiles' concepts (src/shared/orca-profiles.ts + src/main/pty/orca-profiles/, and src/shared/native-chat-agent-profiles.ts). Reusing the bare name will produce confusing greps and possible import collisions in a codebase whose conventions depend on self-documenting filenames.

Secret leakage into logs/telemetry: there is a trust-grant telemetry module (src/main/codex/codex-trust-grant-telemetry.ts) and crash reporting (src/main/crash-reporting/, src/main/ipc/crash-reporting-renderer-breadcrumbs.ts). Profile objects carrying secrets must never be serialised into breadcrumbs, diagnostics (src/main/ipc/diagnostics.ts), or export (src/main/ipc/export.ts). oauth-refresh.ts already models the right discipline: it logs only the HTTP status, never the token.
summary: MAJOR FINDING: the "new" multi-account / API-config switcher feature is ~70% already built in this codebase. There is a mature, test-heavy account subsystem for both providers — `src/main/claude-accounts/` and `src/main/codex-accounts/` — totalling ~27,000 lines (impl+tests) across the accounts/pty subtree, with per-account managed auth directories, app-owned OAuth token refresh, macOS Keychain integration that already mirrors Claude Code 2.1+'s config-dir-scoped service naming, and env-injection-at-spawn as the switching mechanism (NOT global file mutation). The user's headline feature is therefore mostly (a) a rebrand of these paths and (b) adding two missing auth modes (api-key, custom-base-url) plus a per-workspace binding UI on top of an existing seam. VERIFICATION SCOPE — be aware of what I did and did not confirm: I read in full only 5 files (claude-accounts/environment.ts, runtime-paths.ts, managed-auth-path.ts, keychain.ts, oauth-refresh.ts). Everything else below is established from directory listings, line-count inventories, and targeted greps, not from reading the file bodies. Specifically NOT yet read: the `pty:spawn` IPC handler and its env-assembly code path, `src/main/ipc/settings.ts` (schema/migration story), `claude-accounts/service.ts` + `runtime-auth-service.ts` (1125 + 1806 lines), `codex-accounts/service.ts` + `runtime-home-service.ts` (1831 + 1780 lines), and the three docs/claude-*usage*.md files. Those five reads are the required next step before writing code. WHAT IS CONFIRMED BY READING: (1) Switching strategy is already env-injection. `applyClaudeEnvPatch()` in src/main/claude-accounts/environment.ts sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` per spawn and, with `stripAuthEnv`, deletes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK from the child env so an inherited key cannot silently override the selected account. `hasClaudeAuthEnvConflict()` exists to detect exactly that. This is the seam to build on and it validates the env-injection-over-file-swap preference the task statement asked for. (2) Per-account credential isolation on disk already exists: `getClaudeManagedAccountsRoot()` = `join(app.getPath('userData'),'claude-accounts')`, and each account gets `<root>/<accountId>/auth/` containing `.credentials.json` and `oauth-account.json`, written via `writeFileAtomically(..., {mode:0o600})`. Ownership is enforced hard: `resolveOwnedClaudeManagedAuthPath()` rejects symlinks, canonicalises via realpathSync, requires the path be exactly 2 segments below the root matching `<accountId>/auth`, and requires a marker file `.orca-managed-claude-auth` whose contents equal the accountId. There is an `adoptLegacyMarker` option — evidence they have already done one marker migration, so the pattern for renaming the marker exists. (3) The app owns OAuth refresh rather than scraping the CLI: src/main/claude-accounts/oauth-refresh.ts POSTs grant_type=refresh_token to `https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` with public client_id `9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e`, 5-minute expiry skew, via `net.fetch` so Electron's proxy bridge applies. Its comments state the values were verified against `claude` binary 2.1.177. `applyRefreshedToken()` preserves the refresh token unless the server rotates it, and the file comment explicitly names the failure mode the task asked me to reason about: "a single-use refresh token is rotated and persisted atomically, instead of being scraped back after the CLI rotates it (the lossy path that strands stale tokens)". So the token-refresh-race argument is already won and encoded here. (4) Keychain: src/main/claude-accounts/keychain.ts is macOS-only (every function early-returns on non-darwin) and shells out to `/usr/bin/security` with a 3s timeout and a manual timer because Node's execFile timeout alone can leave the callback pending. Two service names: `'Claude Code-credentials'` (the CLI's own, read/written for handoff) and `'Orca Claude Code Managed Credentials'` (the app's own store, keyed by accountId). Critically, `getActiveClaudeService(configDir)` appends `-${sha256(configDir).hex.slice(0,8)}`, with a comment that Claude Code 2.1+ scopes Keychain items by config dir this way. There is NO safeStorage and NO keytar usage in the files I read. (5) Codex switching is CODEX_HOME-based, and it is far more elaborate than Claude's: `CODEX_HOME` appears 623 times across the repo vs `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` 67. src/main/codex-accounts/runtime-home-service.ts (1780 lines, 4544-line test file — the largest test in the subtree) plus src/main/codex/codex-config-mirror.ts, codex-config-settings-{upsert,removal,preservation}.ts, config-toml-trust.ts and a trust-grant ledger (codex-trust-grant-ledger.ts) mean Codex account switching involves materialising a managed CODEX_HOME with a mirrored config.toml and reconciled trust entries. (6) API-key / custom-base-url mode is the genuinely missing piece: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN appears only 2 times repo-wide, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL 12, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY 11, OPENAI_API_KEY 17. Compare CODEX_HOME's 623. The subscription-OAuth path is deeply built; the BYO-key / third-party-gateway path is barely present. That is where the new engineering actually lands. (7) Usage tracking that reads credentials already exists as separate modules: src/main/claude-usage/{scanner,store,types}.ts and src/main/codex-usage/{scanner,store,types}.ts, surfaced over IPC via src/main/ipc/claude-usage.ts and codex-usage.ts, with shared display types src/shared/{claude-usage-types,codex-usage-types,status-bar-usage-mode,usage-percentage-display}.ts. A status-bar usage surface therefore already exists to hang a profile indicator next to. NAMING COLLISION WARNING: `src/shared/orca-profiles.ts` and the directory `src/main/pty/orca-profiles/` already exist and, from their pty location, appear to be terminal/shell profiles — an unrelated concept. Do not name the new entity `Profile` in shared code without disambiguating (suggest `AgentAuthProfile` / `authProfiles` slice).
surface: Credential/auth handling for Claude + Codex, and the foundation it provides for a multi-account / API-config switcher
